harness.song: 120 BPM, 96 PPQN, everything at once: 8 synths with 4-note chords (Cm9/Abmaj7/Fm9/G7sus4, 4-bar clips, notes 2 beats, release approx. 0.85 s), each Saw+Square, 24 dB ladder LPF, sidechain ducking, reverb send: PADA Unison 4+HPF+LFO→LPF+Chorus, PADB Unison 4+Phaser+Delay, PADC HPF+Flanger+Compressor, PADD Bitcrush+SRR, ARP 16ths (2 oct.)+Delay, PADE Unison 4+HPF, FM (DX7, algorithm 5), WT (Wavetable+LFO2). Kit with 8 tracks in a 16th pattern (Kick→Sidechain, Tom +5 and Bell −7 semitones). Audio track: loop at 100 BPM, time-stretched to 120 BPM. Song reverb Mutable and 4 binaural drone tones.
harness.sanity: Output peak −1.5 dBFS, RMS −18 dBFS, 0 clipped samples, no NaN. Pumping on the beat, spectrum plausible, measured.wav attached. Voices: mean 29.7, peak 36, minimum 4. cullVoice(): 0 calls. The result is deterministic (two runs identical). The firmware wrote the song back (--write-back): 16 sounds and 10 clips, all parameters arrived.
harness.notes:
Result: this round needs 83% CPU on average, with peaks at 112%. The peaks fall on the chord changes. There the real Deluge would cull voices.

How it was measured: the real deluge.elf ran unchanged; the tree was not touched and nothing was built. Sequence: resetprg/deluge_main up to registerTasks, then setupStartupSong (loads SONGS/DEFAULT.XML), playButtonPressed, then AudioEngine::routine() per window. FatFS runs on a FAT32 image with 32 KB clusters. Only the hardware is emulated: timers, DMA, SPI, flash, plus a jump over the SDHI initialization.

Limitations:
- Instructions are counted, not cycles. Memory stalls or dual issue can shift the result on the hardware.
- The windows always have 128 samples. That is the most favorable case; smaller windows on the device cost more.
- Windows cut short at clock ticks (10 samples) cost around 200k instructions. That is a high fixed overhead per window, about 6k per voice.

Variant: with a release of 1.6 s the voices rise to 58, the mean to 108% and the peak to 151%.

Digital reverb instead of Mutable: 54k instead of 40k per 128 samples, total 84.3% instead of 82.9%.

Not committed.

problems.problem: Not everything runs at the same time throughout: in the last eighth of every bar the synths are silent.
problems.evidence: My extra script (scratchpad/chk/chk.py) evaluates by 16ths. The 16ths 0–13 cost 84–92% at 28–35 voices, the 16th 14 only 54%, the 16th 15 only 22% at 6 voices. That is 260 windows below 500k instructions (5th percentile 22%). Reason: chords of 2 beats with 0.85 s release end before the end of the bar. The ARP plays only 55% of the time. In the steady state the mean is about 89%, not 83%.
problems.fix: In make_sd.py, stretch the chord and ARP notes over the whole bar (384 ticks, legato). In addition, report a mean only over the windows in which all 16 sounds have voices.

problems.problem: The claim about culling is wrong: the real Deluge would cull constantly, not only at the peaks.
problems.evidence: getLastRunTimeforCurrentTask() returns durationStats.average of the audio task. The harness empties taskManager, so 0 comes back. In cullVoices() the soft cull starts from 80 samples (62.5% of a 128-sample window), the hard cull from 112 samples (87.5%). At 89–92% sustained load the device would therefore make hard culls all the time.
problems.fix: Intercept getLastRunTimeforCurrentTask and return the emulated duration of the previous routine() call (instructions / 400 MHz). Then report both values: the run with culling (culls, voices) and the demand without culling.

problems.problem: Whether all tracks play is not checked per run.
problems.evidence: Only the extra script shows it: 16 sounds have voices. 6 pads play with 4 voices 90% of the time, one synth with 2.5 on average, the ARP with at most 2. All 8 kit rows are active (10–100% of the time).
problems.fix: Add the voices per sound (activeVoices by Sound*) to result.json.

problems.problem: The Digital comparison measures different bars.
problems.evidence: Digital runs over 2 bars, Mutable over 4. So the comparison 84.3% against 82.9% mixes the reverb difference with the chord difference.
problems.fix: Measure the same number of bars or compare only the reverb area (54k against 40k).

verdict.crossCheck: The rerun is identical: 962,920 instructions per block (peak 1,303,588), 36 voices, 0 culls, −1.5/−18 dBFS, no NaN. The whole AudioEngine::routine() is counted, including ticks and doSomeOutputting. The playback task and cluster loading run separately and cost only 92 per block. The areas add up exactly to the total (963,013). Voice::render is inlined into Sound::render, so the attribution to "voices" is correct. Instructions against voices: 28k per voice plus 126k fixed, r=0.98. Filter bench (ARM): LpLadder 252.6k over around 22.5 LPF voices gives 11.2k per voice; the bench (LP24 res30 mono) shows 10.8k. HpLadder: 78k over 10.8 voices gives 7.2k, the bench 7.7k. Oscillator bench: saw unison 4 costs 6.3k, simple waves 1.6k. Times the voices that gives around 179k, measured 178k. The benches for effects, reverb, delay and drone were not rerun.
